card.title: Cubical Expansion, Superficial Expansion and Their Relation with Linear Expansion

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Every edge of a heated solid obeys $\Delta L = \alpha L \Delta T$, so area and volume follow automatically: $A = A_0(1+2\alpha\Delta T)$ and $V = V_0(1+3\alpha\Delta T)$ — the binomial's higher terms vanish because αΔT is minuscule. Hence the **superficial coefficient β = 2α** and the **cubical coefficient γ = 3α**, with the ratio chain $\alpha:\beta:\gamma = 1:2:3$.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - A = A₀(1+βΔT); β = 2α - V = V₀(1+γΔT); γ = 3α - α : β : γ = 1 : 2 : 3

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Isotropic Material: γ = 3α and β = 2α only for isotropic solids. Crystalline anisotropic materials have different α along different axes.  ·  Small ΔT: Formulas assume constant α over temperature range. For large ΔT, α may vary.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The coefficient of cubical expansion is three times the coefficient of linear expansion."

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **The 1:2:3 chain:** α : β : γ = 1 : 2 : 3 — memorise it and half the numericals solve themselves.  ·  **Binomial truncation:** (1+αΔT)² ≈ 1+2αΔT only because αΔT is tiny.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Expanding in Two and Three Dimensions A heated plate grows in area; a heated block grows in volume. Because every edge obeys the same linear law, the area and volume coefficients follow automatically: β = 2α and γ = 3α. One measurement of α pins down the whole thermal fingerprint.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Superficial (area) expansion A plate of area $A_0$ heated by ΔT: $$A_T = A_0(1 + \beta \Delta T), \qquad \beta = \frac{\Delta A / A_0}{\Delta T}$$ β = coefficient of superficial expansion, unit K⁻¹.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A copper cube of volume 500 cm³ at 0 °C is heated to 200 °C (α = 1.7×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹). Find ΔV.** — γ = 5.1×10⁻⁵ K⁻¹; ΔV = 5.1×10⁻⁵ × 500×10⁻⁶ × 200 = 5.1×10⁻⁹ m³ = 5.1 cm³... check: 5.1×10⁻⁵×5×10⁻⁴×200 = 5.1×10⁻⁶ m³ = 5.1 cm³.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The β = 2α and γ = 3α derivations are the likely 3m questions.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **All expansion is linear expansion wearing different clothes** — area and volume laws derive from the edge law.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: β = 2α; γ = 3α; A = A₀(1+βΔT); V = V₀(1+γΔT).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A heated hole in a plate expands too — the hole behaves as if made of the surrounding material.
